images.caption: Memorial outside Sherborne Abbey This Victorian memorial was erected in 1884 in memory of George Digby Wingfield Digby, Sherborne Abbey's greatest 19th century benefactor.  At the four corners are bronze statuettes of St Aldhelm, Bishop Roger, Abbot Bradford and Sir Walter Raleigh.

images.caption: Memorial outside Sherborne Abbey The Digby Memorial, situated outside the Abbey, is a memorial to George Digby who provided a lot of funding for renovation work during the 19th century. It was built in 1884 and features statues of St Aldhelm, Bishop Roger of Salisbury (Roger de Caen), Abbot Bradford and Sir Walter Raleigh.  Thanks to Wikipedia for this information.

images.caption: Sherborne Abbey (St. Mary), 27 July 2015. Founded as cathedral in 705 but seat was moved in 1075. It had already become a Benedictine Monastery in 998. Some Saxon work remains but most of current structure built 11th Century Norman and rebuilt/remodelled in 15th Century Perpendicular. Restored mid 19th Century Victorian. Pictured is the blocked probably late 10th Century Saxon doorway on the west front.

images.caption: Sherborne Abbey (St. Mary), 27 July 2015. Founded as cathedral in 705 but seat was moved in 1075. It had already become a Benedictine Monastery in 998. images.caption:
This is a wonderful Elizabeth and Tudor mansion located half a mile from the equally wonderful town of Sherborne, north Dorset.
It is a very large mansion, which is very beautiful both inside and out, but it is not especially intimidating in size, unlike Buckingham Palace. 
It has been the home of the Digby Family since 1617.

It is also situated in wonderful gardens, also worth a visit.
